title: add jsonschema strict response_format + improved validation/errors (openai-compat)
author: Marta Chen
title_line: Add jsonschema strict response_format + improved validation/errors (OpenAI-compat)
description:
Motivation: Surface-level compatibility with OpenAI's response_format + strict/jsonschema validation is required by several customers to enforce structured outputs for downstream tooling and auditing. This PR adds a stable API surface for request.response_format=json_schema and implements strict-mode behavior (reject-on-violations) with improved error reporting that maps back to prompt/schema.

Scope: 1) request API flag response_format: 'json_schema' and 'json_schema_strict' (backwards-compatible with current response_format values) 2) server-side schema validation using the new lightweight validator (schema idempotency + path-aware errors) 3) deterministic error payloads with machine-friendly error_codes and human-friendly messages 4) OpenAI-compat mapping layer so existing callers using openai-style 'response_format' and "response_schema" keys still work 5) tests, docs, and a canary rollout plan.

Implementation notes: - The runtime now recognizes response_format=json_schema and will attempt to coerce/validate model output against the provided JSON Schema. - Strict mode (json_schema_strict) rejects completions that do not parse/validate; the rejection path returns a 422 with a structured error that includes schema path, validator keyword and sample fix suggestion. - Non-strict mode attempts a best-effort repair: if the model returns trailing text or minor formatting issues we run the sanitizer that extracts the JSON payload and re-validate; if still invalid we surface warning metadata but return the best-effort JSON with a metadata.errors array. - Added an OpenAI-compat layer: if the request uses "response_schema" or legacy response_format values we translate to the new internal representation and record telemetry tags for migration. - Careful perf: validation is done post-generation and is async-safe; short-circuiting is used for simple schemas to avoid CPU spikes. - Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless response_format explicitly set.

Testing & rollout: - Unit + integration tests for valid/invalid schemas and mixed streaming scenarios. - Synthetic perf benchmark shows ~1.8ms median overhead for typical small schemas, 95th percentile under 10ms for larger schemas. - Canary rollout: traffic tagged for schema-enabled customers routed to a small subset of runtime nodes; automatic fallbacks to non-strict path if repeated validation failures are observed.

Related: ENG-4572, docs PR will follow that updates the API reference, and a provider SDK patch (python/ts/go) to expose response_format helpers.

Checklist: - [x] API flag parsing and OpenAI-compat mapping - [x] Validator implementation and test coverage - [x] Error payload format agreed with SRE/Docs - [x] Canary config and fallback policy - [x] Perf tests and cost regression analysis - [x] Updated integration tests with streaming + schema failures

Rollout notes: Canary starts at 1% on 2025-09-24, ramp to 25% after 48h if error rates stable. If strict-mode rejection spikes >1% for a customer route we automatically fallback that route to non-strict mode and emit an alert for the on-call SRE.

merge_summary: Squashed 9 commits into main. Adds jsonschema strict-mode response_format with OpenAI compatibility mapping, validator, sanitizer, tests, docs, and canary config.
release_notes: Added response_format=json_schema and response_format=json_schema_strict to enforce structured outputs via JSON Schema.
Strict mode returns 422 on validation failure with structured error payload (schema path + validator keyword + suggested fix).
Non-strict mode returns best-effort JSON with metadata.errors when validation fails; sanitizer attempts to extract JSON from model output.
OpenAI compatibility layer translates legacy response_schema keys to the new internal representation.
Canary rollout and automatic fallback policies included.
